defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: line 17: expanduser always prepends ~/, mangling absolute NETRC paths
line 11: empty NETRC string passes and resolves to home dir, netrc() crashes
line 17: relative paths like subdir/.netrc or ./local/.netrc resolve under ~ instead of cwd
test only covers bare filename; no absolute/empty/missing path tests
docstring doesn't describe NETRC env var behavior
pre-existing: account field from authenticators() discarded
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` unconditionally prepends `~/`, mangling absolute `NETRC` paths. `NETRC="/tmp/.netrc"` becomes `~/tmp/.netrc` → `/home/user/tmp/.netrc`.
votes.justification: The review identifies the expanduser call that always prepends ~/ as mangling absolute NETRC paths. That is the same cause and behavior as the known defect, at the right line.
